questions.cardText:
[History] Where did the word “sandwich” originate?
A. United States
B. Britain
C. France
Answer: B. The word “sandwich” comes from John Montagu, the 4th Earl of Sandwich in Britain. He popularized placing meat between two slices of bread to eat without stopping his work or, in some accounts, gambling.
questions.de: Nach welchem britischen Adligen des 18. Jahrhunderts ist das Sandwich benannt?
questions.en: After which 18th-century British nobleman is the sandwich named?

timeline.labelEn: John Montagu, 4th Earl of Sandwich, after whom the sandwich is named
timeline.labelDe: John Montagu, 4. Earl of Sandwich, nach dem das Sandwich benannt ist

questions.notes: Card's answer (Britain) stands; asked for the Earl the explanation names, which pins the word's origin. Lifespan at year precision: his birth date is given as 3/14 November 1718 (Old/New Style).

questions.cardText:
[Ecology] What is a keystone species?
A. A species that helps maintain the structure of an ecological community
B. A species at the top of the food chain
C. The most abundant species in a community
Answer: A. Generally, a keystone species has a large influence on its environment relative to its abundance in that environment.
questions.de: Wie nennt man in der Ökologie eine Art, die im Verhältnis zu ihrer Häufigkeit einen unverhältnismäßig großen Einfluss auf ihre Umwelt hat und die Struktur einer Lebensgemeinschaft erhält?
questions.en: In ecology, what is a species called that has a disproportionately large effect on its environment relative to its abundance, maintaining the structure of its community?

timeline.labelEn: Zoologist Robert T. Paine introduces the concept of the keystone species
timeline.labelDe: Der Zoologe Robert T. Paine führt das Konzept der Schlüsselart ein
